question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Temporal degron window to separate establishment from maintenance
ideas.description: Use an inducible degron (auxin or dTAG) to remove Fos or Jun at different times after a stimulus pulse, then re-stimulate. If memory requires AP-1 only during establishment, late removal leaves re-induction intact; if it requires ongoing AP-1, late removal erases it.

ideas.title: Occupancy versus chromatin persistence time course
ideas.description: Run CUT&Tag for Fos/Jun alongside ATAC-seq and H3K27ac at memory-gene enhancers across a time course after pulse withdrawal. If accessibility and H3K27ac outlast AP-1 occupancy, the chromatin state, not the transcription factor, is carrying the memory.

ideas.title: Mitotic bookmarking and heritable memory
ideas.description: Image whether AP-1 stays on mitotic chromosomes and combine barcoded lineage tracing with a pulse to ask whether the primed state is inherited by daughter cells. Persistence through division would support a heritable, cell-intrinsic memory rather than a signal re-supplied each time.

ideas.title: Heterodimer composition swap knock-ins
ideas.description: Replace c-Jun with JunB, or Fos with Fra1 or ATF3, at the endogenous locus and compare the strength and duration of memory after a pulse. If memory depends on partner identity rather than total AP-1 activity, specific dimer composition, not just presence, encodes the memory.

ideas.title: Locus-specific synthetic recruitment and hysteresis
ideas.description: Pulse a tethered AP-1 fragment, or a dimerizer-recruited Jun, onto a silent reporter and release it, then monitor whether the reporter stays active. Combining this with dose ramps up and down tests whether AP-1 alone can produce a stable, hysteretic switch at a locus.

candidates: Auxin/dTAG degron removal of Fos or Jun at defined windows after a stimulus pulse, then re-stimulation readout
CUT&Tag time course of Fos/Jun occupancy after stimulus withdrawal at memory-gene enhancers
ATAC-seq and H3K27ac time course after pulse withdrawal to see if accessibility outlasts AP-1 binding
Tethered dCas9 or dimerizer recruitment of a c-Jun/Fos fragment to a silent reporter, pulsed and then released
Optogenetic AP-1 (opto-Fos/Jun) pulses of defined duration and frequency to test encoding of memory
Hysteresis test: ramp stimulus dose up and down and compare thresholds for AP-1 target induction
Mathematical model of AP-1 positive feedback and bistability, fit to time-course data and tested with predicted perturbations
Protein half-life measurement of Fos and Jun under pulses (pulse-chase, cycloheximide, SNAP tags) to test if protein persistence is the carrier
Mitotic bookmarking: imaging whether AP-1 stays on mitotic chromosomes and whether memory survives division
Barcoded clonal lineage tracing combined with a pulse to test whether memory is heritable across cell divisions
Heterodimer composition swap knock-ins (c-Jun vs JunB vs Fra1, ATF3) to see if memory depends on partner identity
CRISPR screen for genes required for faster re-induction of AP-1 targets but not for first response
Proteomics of AP-1 chromatin-associated cofactors (p300/CBP, BRD4, SWI/SNF) before and after pulse to identify memory-linked complexes
Inhibition of p300/CBP or BRD4 during the post-pulse window to test whether acetylation writers maintain memory
DNA methylation and 5hmC profiling at AP-1 sites after repeated pulses
3D chromatin (Micro-C or HiChIP) looping persistence at AP-1 enhancers after stimulus removal
Single-cell Fos reporter tracking with live imaging to quantify re-induction speed and heterogeneity after priming
Nuclear condensate or phase-separation analysis of AP-1 clusters persisting after stimulus
Lineage-tracing mouse model (Fos-CreERT2 or TRAP) with injury or stress pulse and later rechallenge in tissue
Ex vivo primary cell trained-immunity-style assay: prime with a pulse, rest, then rechallenge and measure AP-1 target output
Synthetic minimal circuit in engineered cells with inducible AP-1 to test whether a bare feedback loop can store a pulse
